states.name: on-dark
states.gap: The dot rows are the same width in both images: 254 px under 'definately', 206 under 'recieved' and 'comittee', 78 under 'Teh'. A sets the words about 1.5% wider (26.0 px per cell against 25.6, 1664 px against 1638), so its mark stops short of each word. Under 'definately' the row covers about 97.7% of a roughly 260 px word, and the tail of the 'y' hangs past the last dot. The gap between the lowest ink of the 'y' and the top dot row is also 1 px tighter: 2 blank rows (y=45–46) against 3 (y=44–46).
states.gapTheirs: B has no mark gap of its own. Ink (#CF807E core, #7F5352/#805452 edges), 8 px pitch, 6 rows (y=47–52), dot shape and marked words match A pixel for pixel. B's only difference is that its dot edge pixels sit about 2% darker (#7F5352 against #845655) and a few blend toward #1E1C1C, so each dot looks very slightly harder.
states.verdict: The mark itself is the same in both. They share the same salmon dots on the same 8 px pitch, 6 rows deep and 12 px under the baseline, and they mark the same four words while leaving DRAFFT alone. What decides it is the fit: B's dots cover their words from end to end, while A's stop a few pixels short, so the tail of the 'y' in 'definately' hangs past the mark. A writer won't consciously notice this, but A's squiggle looks slightly undersized and sits slightly closer to the descenders.

states.gapTheirs: Hardly any gap in the mark. A's dots cover 254 of the 256 px of 'definately' (10 cells × 25.6); B's cover 254 of 260. states.verdict: On the mark itself these two are the same: identical #ed766b dots, 6 px across on an 8 px pitch, in rows 47–52 and 121–126, under the same four words, with 'DRAFFT' left alone. Both keep the dots at full ink under the dimmed out-of-focus words (#c6c4c2), so neither lets a typo fade into the grey. The one thing a writer might catch is that B's dotted rule stops a few pixels before the last letter of long words, like a correction that ran out of ink. A's dots end almost at the edge of each word, so A wins, narrowly.

A's dots always reach the last letter, sometimes 6 px past it. B's dots stop 3 px short of the tail of 'definately', so the mark looks like it missed the last letter.

states.verdict: For a writer the mark is the same in both: a quiet row of salmon dots 12 px below the baseline, under the same four typos, leaving the all-caps DRAFFT alone. Neither one looks like a squiggle that nags you while you type. The whole difference is sub-pixel: B shades the top and bottom of each dot to half strength, so its dots read as squashed, fainter beads next to A's even round ones. It's a tiny gap, but A's dot is the one that holds its shape.
